newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB lent 3.16 bln yen to racketeer-linked firm-MOF.
newsitem.headline: DKB lent 3.16 bln yen to racketeer-linked firm-MOF.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd lent 3.16 billion yen to a firm linked to a racketeer to buy shares in Japan's "Big Four" securities houses, the Finance Ministry said in a report presented to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on Friday.
The brokerages are Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd 8601 T, Nikko Securities Co Ltd, and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, it said.
The report, presented to a meeting of the LDP's financial panel, said DKB lent a total of 27.5 billion yen to Yoshinori Koike and a company owned by him.

Yoshinori Koike is the younger brother of corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike. Both brothers were arrested earlier this month on suspicion of taking about 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura.
Japanese media have reported that the loans provided by DKB were used to help the elder Koike buy shares in Nomura, which allowed him to put pressure on the firm to give him preferential treatment.
DKB has declined comments on the media reports.

The ministry said in the report that DKB provided the 3.16 billion yen worth of loans in February, 1989, to Koike's company, which then bought the shares in the four brokerages and gave the shares to the bank to hold as collateral for the loans.

The figure of 27.5 billion yen refers to the accumulated amount of loans to Koike and his company over a period of time. Of that amount, DKB has said that its loans outstanding to Yoshinori Koike and his company total about 7.5 billion yen.

The Finance Ministry report also said that in addition to the loans used to buy shares, DKB lent 1.57 billion yen to the racketeer-linked firm as funds to invest in a golf course, while a non-bank financial institution, Daiwa Shinyo, lent the firm 1.6 billion yen in November 1990.
The report said that DKB took over the loans provided by Daiwa Shinyo in 1991.
It also said that DKB set aside loan loss provisions of seven billion yen by March 1997 on the loans made to Yoshinori Koike and his company.

In the report, the ministry said it suspected that in 1990 DKB concealed the full amount of loans to Yoshinori Koike and his company by indirectly lending additional money to them so they could pay back part of the loans.

The ministry also said it also suspected that in 1994, Daiwa Shinyo, which has a close business relationship with DKB, lent 616 million yen to the company owned by Yoshinori Koike, aimed at concealing his problem loans.
DKB has admitted it may have concealed details of the loans ahead of inspections by the Finance Ministry in 1990 and 1994. It has also said officials involved in any wrongdoing will be punished.
Last Friday, DKB announced that top executives including its president and chairman would resign as of the end June to take responsibility for the racketeer scandal.
